extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, historians, inventors, patent attorneys, and USPTO staff consulting historical patent issuance records
extracted.subtask_description: An alphabetical index of patents issued in 1877 listing the invention title, patentee name(s), patent number, issue date, Monthly Volume reference, and Official Gazette reference. Useful for locating and cross-referencing issued patents from that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention or discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The title or name of the invention or discovery as the index entry (e.g., "Collar, Horse", "Cooking apparatus", "Cotton-gin feeder and cleaner").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are the principal headwords used to identify the subject-matter of the patent; they include variants, hyphenated forms, and sub-entries (e.g., multiple forms of "Corset" listed under one heading). Headwords may include parenthetical clarifiers or compound names. The index continues alphabetically across pages (marked "Alphabetical list of inventions—Continued").

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of patentee
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor(s) or patentee(s) associated with the patent (listed alongside the invention title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically shown as personal names or combinations (e.g., "J. K. Pumpelly and E. Collins", "H. W. and C. F. Whitney"); may include multiple parties separated by commas or conjunctions. Used to identify ownership/credit for the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No.
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent number assigned to the issued patent (column labeled "No.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric patent identifiers are given (e.g., "192,378", "197,492"). These are the official patent numbers used to retrieve the full patent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue date of the patent (column labeled "Date").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are shown in month/day/year format (e.g., "July 10, 1877", "Dec. 18, 1877"); formatting varies (abbreviated months, occasional OCR/printing inconsistencies). This is the official grant/issue date for the patent number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly volume
rubrics_metrics.description: A numeric reference under the heading "Monthly volume" associated with each patent entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains numbers (often three- or four-digit) that appear to reference the monthly publication or index location (examples: "903", "531", "402"). Values appear in a dedicated column and may assist locating the patent in monthly reports or bound volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: A short numeric code/reference under the heading "Official Gazette" shown for each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values are small integers (commonly "11", "12", sometimes "13") listed in a dedicated column; these indicate the Official Gazette issue or column reference in which the patent was announced or summarized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Index organization principle: entries are ordered alphabetically by invention title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document explicitly presents an "Alphabetical list of inventions" and includes continuation markers; adjacent entries and page breaks preserve alphabetical order across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references ('See' entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of cross-reference notes ("See ...") to direct from one headword to a related headword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several entries include 'See' cross-references (e.g., "Cup: See Beer-cooler.", "Coupling: See Belt-coupling."). These direct the reader to alternate or preferred index terms and indicate synonymy or related classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subentries and variant forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple related sub-entries or variant forms listed under a main heading (e.g., many types of "Corset" entries like "Corset, Abdominal clasp", "Corset, skirt-supporter").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index groups related constructions and variants under a general heading and enumerates specific forms or functions. This shows the index captures scope and subtypes of inventions rather than only a single label per patent.
